Treatment summary
Patient presented following a rear-end motor vehicle collision with complaints of neck
and low back pain and stiffness. The reported injuries are consistent with the
mechanism and force of the impact. Care was delivered over 23 visits, consisting of
manual therapy, supervised exercise, and home program instruction, and followed an
expected course with symptoms gradually easing and visit frequency tapering as
function improved. Most of the clinical picture rests on the patient's subjective pain
reports, as cervical and lumbar range-of-motion and neurological screening were
unremarkable and imaging studies showed no acute abnormality. The patient mentioned a
minor strain to the same region several years ago, which the patient reports resolved
completely without lasting limitation. Billing records reflect single charges for each
service with no duplicated or repeated entries. Prognosis is fair with conitnued home
exercise, and the patient was advised to return if symptoms recur or worsen.
